## Verdict: REJECT (one acceptance criterion is not met: two first-run walkthroughs ask the AC/DC question without stating the expected answer)

This PR is not ready to merge: acceptance criterion twenty-two requires every first-run walkthrough that asks the AC/DC question to state the expected answer of 2 albums, and two walkthroughs do not.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

- VC-122: FAIL (critical) — Each first-run walkthrough lists Docker with Compose and an Anthropic API key as prerequisites. It starts the `examples/mysql-demo` container and points SQL Lens at it through a `mysql+pymysql://` URL. It keeps the Chinook sample questions, and wherever it asks the AC/DC question it states the expected answer, 2 albums. The walkthroughs are, at minimum: - the README quick start; - step 2 of `docs/external/getting-started.md`; - the fast path and the manual install in `docs/external/install-claude-desktop-windows.md`. Where these pages explain connecting to the reader's own database, they say SQL Lens needs a MySQL 8.0+ server. The README quick-start heading, the getting-started introduction and `docs/external/index.md` no longer promise a 60-second or under-a-minute first run. Any first-run duration they state includes pulling the `mysql:8.0` image and loading the demo. [README.md] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 22, so it counts. Most of the criterion holds: README.md:20 lists Docker with Compose and an Anthropic API key and says the first run takes a few minutes including the mysql:8.0 pull; README.md:31 uses mysql+pymysql and states 'The answer is 2'; getting-started.md:3,8-9,28-38 and install-claude-desktop-windows.md:11-14,26-31,121-140 cover Docker, the container and the mysql+pymysql URL; 'MySQL 8.0+' appears where own-database connection is explained (README:33, getting-started:96, Windows:12,78); no 60-second promise in the README heading, getting-started intro or index.md. But the criterion requires 'wherever it asks the AC/DC question it states the expected answer, 2 albums'. docs/external/getting-started.md:56 (step 4, the first-run walkthrough) asks 'Using sqllens, how many albums did AC/DC release?' with no expected answer (lines 54-60 never state 2). docs/external/install-claude-desktop-windows.md:70 (Verify the connection, part of the fast path) asks the AC/DC question and likewise gives no answer (lines 69-72). Both are counterexamples to the stated-answer requirement; the matching question in the README does state it, but that does not excuse the others. No sibling criterion excuses this.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` lines 44 to 50: the "Not covered" paragraph of the module docstring wraps oddly after the deletion ("A catalog" ends one line and "table that holds credentials" starts the next). The text is still accurate. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `tests/unit/test_rls_views.py` lines 312 to 319: no test calls `verify_base_tables(..., dialect="sqlite")`, and no unknown-dialect row asserts that the cursor issues no query. Criterion nine asks for both the refusal and no query on the cursor; only the refusal is pinned. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-66: FAIL (suggestion) — The first question creates ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma/ for ChromaDB memory, matching the demo config's persist_dir resolved relative to the repository root. [examples/mysql-demo/README.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  README.md:42-44 says the first question creates ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma/. sqllens.toml:24 sets persist_dir = "./examples/mysql-demo/chroma" (cwd-relative; matches only when run from repo root, as the README commands do). ChromaAgentMemory is lazy: __init__ (agent_memory.py:107-128) does no I/O and PersistentClient is only created in _get_client (:136-152). But the documented command `sqllens serve -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml` runs run_preflight(cfg) by default (cli.py:241-249) before run(cfg); run_preflight runs probe_memory (preflight.py:245-257), which does persist_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (preflight.py:188). So the directory is created at serve startup (and by validate --check-memory), before any question; the first question is not what creates it. Only the Chroma store files inside would be created lazily at first touch. Repo rule AGENTS.md 'Claims must match the code' / 'Boot vs. lazy / first-call' requires behavioral doc claims to match the code; text unchanged in base and head.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

- VC-39: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — From sqlglot 30.22 the MySQL tokenizer ends a block comment at the first */ [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The claim is the last sentence of docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:54 ('From 30.22 the MySQL tokenizer also ends a block comment at the first */, as MySQL does.'). It is a library claim, but the item has no dependency_sources and the views contain no sqlglot source (Glob for **/sqlglot* in the head view found nothing). The claim cannot be verified from the views alone. Not run: reading sqlglot 30.22's sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py (and tokens.py) block-comment handling, and comparing it with the pre-30.22 release.

  </details>

- VC-41: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — DESCRIBE parses as exp.Command (rejected) under the guard; with PRAGMA dropped the doc still lists every rejected introspection form [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Behavior: DESCRIBE is rejected under mysql. assert_select_only (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:545-560) raises UnsafeSqlError for any root not in _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES (:276-282). But the claim's mechanism is inaccurate: sqlglot (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlglot/parser.py:1203 STATEMENT_PARSERS TokenType.DESCRIBE -> _parse_describe, :3641 returns exp.Describe; mysql.py has no override, only EXPLAIN->DESCRIBE at :106) parses DESCRIBE to exp.Describe, not exp.Command. The doc line docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:61 says DESCRIBE and non-allowlisted SHOW 'parse as exp.Command / non-allowlisted exp.Show roots', which is imprecise for DESCRIBE (outcome, rejection, is right). That line is text the PR changed (base also mentions DESCRIBE at base line 62 with PRAGMA), so it is not a usable requirement source, and no unchanged file requires the claimed Command parse; so neither FAIL nor INVALID can be established. Whether other introspection forms are fully listed was not exhaustively checked; the doc lists DESCRIBE and non-allowlisted SHOW (and CALL at :58).

  </details>

- VC-60: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — During first-start loading the mysql image runs a temporary server with no TCP listener, so the TCP healthcheck as chinook_reader against Chinook.Album only passes after both init scripts finished. [examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml:16-31 matches the claim's text: the healthcheck runs `mysql -h127.0.0.1 -uchinook_reader -pchinook_reader -e 'SELECT 1 FROM Chinook.Album LIMIT 1'`, i.e. over TCP, as the demo user, against Chinook. The claim's truth depends on the mysql:8.0 image's docker-entrypoint.sh starting its temporary server with --skip-networking. No dependency_sources were supplied and a Glob for docker-entrypoint.sh in the head view found none, so I could not read the entrypoint. I did not run the image or inspect it with docker. I recall the upstream entrypoint using --skip-networking, but that is not evidence I read.

  </details>

- VC-76: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — sqlglot exp.Table.db returns the schema qualifier name as a string (empty when unqualified) for MySQL-parsed tables, including quoted identifiers [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The item has no dependency_sources. A Glob for **/sqlglot*/**/expressions* in the head view found nothing, and a Glob for **/sqlglot/expressions.py over / found nothing. I could not read Table.db in the locked sqlglot version. The use site is src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:273, `(table.db or "").lower()`, which tolerates an empty value. Whether Table.db returns a string for quoted MySQL identifiers is unverified.

  </details>

- VC-86: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Patching socket.socket.connect and connect_ex catches every network connect validate could make (pymysql and any LLM/HTTP client use socket.socket.connect, not create_connection on a subclass bypassing it) [tests/unit/test_cli.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/unit/test_cli.py:143-169 patches socket.socket.connect and connect_ex with a refusing stub (lines 157-158) and asserts no attempts during `validate` without --check-db. The claim depends on how pymysql (connections.py connect()) and stdlib socket.create_connection behave at runtime. The item has no dependency_sources, and no pymysql or stdlib source is in the views, so I could not read them as the rules require. Copies of pymysql exist in other venvs on the host, but those are outside the supplied views and dependency_sources, so I did not use them. The claim is also absolute (every network connect, any LLM/HTTP client). Async or C-level clients may not route through the patched Python-level methods. I did not trace those clients. Missing evidence: pymysql and stdlib socket source via dependency_sources.

  </details>

- VC-114: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `examples/mysql-demo/` holds a `sqllens.toml`, a Docker Compose file, a `README.md`, the user-creation init script and `Chinook_MySql.sql`. `.gitattributes` exempts `Chinook_MySql.sql` from line-ending normalization. Both the committed blob (`git cat-file -p HEAD:examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql`) and the checked-out file have SHA-256 `02a1835417c3ea19bff64e1d1f22be738ce51b3f88b0473c24eebff9a3ccde4b` and are 616,450 bytes. [.gitattributes]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Verified: head inventory.json lists examples/mysql-demo/{Chinook_MySql.sql (blob, size 616450), README.md, compose.yaml, demo-user.sql, sqllens.toml}; .gitattributes:4 has '* text=auto eol=lf' and :7 'examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql -text', which is a later, more specific line and exempts the file from normalization. Criterion 14 counts (criteria.json has criterion 14 as a {criterion,text} object). Not verified: the SHA-256 02a18354...de4b of the committed blob and the checked-out file. I have no tool to hash the file (no shell; the 616,450-byte file cannot be hashed by reading), and inventory.json lists only the git blob SHA-1 cdbd482f..., not a SHA-256. The command not run is `git cat-file -p HEAD:examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql | sha256sum` plus `sha256sum` on the working file. Size matches 616450.

  </details>

- VC-116: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — With `SQLLENS_LLM__API_KEY` set: 1. Start the demo container with `docker compose` from a fresh checkout and wait until it is ready. 2. Run `sqllens validate --check-db -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml`. It exits 0. 3. Query the demo database as the demo config's user for the number of albums whose artist is `AC/DC`. It returns 2. The demo config keeps `read_only = true`, and its ChromaDB `persist_dir` lies under `examples/mysql-demo/`. A run that cannot use Docker ends Blocked on this criterion. [examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml:16,24]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Static parts verified in examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml: read_only = true (line 16), persist_dir = "./examples/mysql-demo/chroma" (line 24). Files present: compose.yaml, Chinook_MySql.sql, demo-user.sql, README.md. The runtime steps (docker compose start, `sqllens validate --check-db` exit 0, AC/DC album count = 2) require Docker and an API key; I did not run them. Per the criterion, a run that cannot use Docker ends Blocked. Criteria file not separately relied on.

  </details>

- VC-118: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt` has a section for `examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql`. The section names the upstream project, the v1.4.5 release and its URL, and it carries the upstream copyright line and permission notice verbatim. [LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criterion 18 counted from criteria.json (valid list of {criterion,text}). LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt:284-300 has a section for examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql naming The Chinook Database (github.com/lerocha/chinook-database), release v1.4.5 with its release URL, plus a 'Copyright (c) 2008-2024 Luis Rocha' line and an MIT permission notice. The structural parts of the claim hold. 'Verbatim' against upstream LICENSE.md cannot be checked from the views: the repo has no copy of upstream LICENSE.md (Chinook_MySql.sql:8 only links to it), no dependency_sources were supplied, and I did not fetch https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database/blob/v1.4.5/LICENSE.md. The year range in the copyright line (2008-2024) and the paragraph breaks (the notice paragraph at line 299 is followed directly by the warranty disclaimer at line 300 with no blank line) are unverified. Missing evidence: upstream v1.4.5 LICENSE.md text.

  </details>

</details>
